rationale: Both catch the two confirmed ground-truth bugs (varlen_func None crash, FA3 SM90 gating) and go well beyond GT with plausible novel findings (per-layer kernel loading, duplication, Blackwell gating ambiguity). X's precision is hurt by highly specific, hard-to-verify external claims (exact HF Hub commit hashes across two repos, exact kernels-library internal error text) that read as fabricated confabulation, and its 'version=1 defeats the PR's purpose' framing is actually contradicted by the maintainer's own clarification in the GT thread. Y sticks closer to statically-verifiable, quoted code evidence, explicitly tracks which GT threads were already resolved (showing real engagement with review history), and ships copy-paste-ready `suggestion` diffs, making it both more grounded and more actionable.
